findings_coverage: Openly accessible evidence above 10 eV is theory only, to 50 eV: Itikawa et al. 1986 Table 5.1 reproduces Onda & Truhlar (1979/1980) and Rumble, Truhlar & Morrison (1983) for j0->2, 0->4, 0->6 at 10-50 eV [P1:itikawa1986_table5_1]; Siegel, Dehmer & Dill 1978 (ANL-78-65) gives j0->2/4/6 to 30 eV [P1:siegel_dehmer_dill_1978].

The only measured rotational ICS above 10 eV found is the preliminary Tanaka, Boesten & Shimamura 1980 conference/private-communication set (5, 10, 20 eV), reproduced secondarily in Itikawa 1986; the compilers state it must be confirmed [P1:tanaka_boesten_shimamura_1980].

Share of the held j0->2 table rate above 50 eV (recomputed by the check from repo TABLE6 with hold beyond 10 eV): 50.77 % at L = 45 eV and 64.77 % at L = 60 eV; above 200 eV 0.98 % / 4.06 %; above 266 eV 0.14 % / 0.99 % [P1 check correction].

Every source whose stated range reaches the lane-01 E_req is closed / abstract-only: Kutz & Meyer 1995 (theory, 0.01-1000 eV) [P1:kutz_meyer_1995], Bhattacharyya & Goswami 1982 (eikonal theory, ICS 20-200 eV) [P1:bhattacharyya_goswami_1982], Gote & Ehrhardt 1995 (the only measurement: state-to-state DCS 10-200 eV, 10-160 deg) [P1:gote_ehrhardt_1995], Choi et al. 1979 (50-500 eV; rotational tabulation not shown) [P1:choi_poe_sun_shan_1979].
findings_join_shape_conflicts: At the 10 eV join every independent j0->2 value lies above Song Table 6 (ratios 1.22-1.44; see computed.P1), with no stated uncertainty anywhere, so C3 cannot be evaluated.

Theory shape 10-50 eV contradicts the flat hold: j0->2 falls to 0.42-0.43 of its 10 eV value by 50 eV; j0->4 dips at 20 eV then rises to 1.0-1.4x; j0->6 (absent from the table set) grows to 0.24-0.34e-16 cm2 at 30-50 eV [P1:itikawa1986_table5_1]. Kutz & Meyer and Gote & Ehrhardt abstracts report rotational rainbows / large angular-momentum transfer at higher energy [P1:kutz_meyer_1995, P1:gote_ehrhardt_1995].

The Born point-quadrupole (Gerjuoy & Stein 1955) estimate is a slow-electron threshold theory (abstract), not a usable envelope above 10 eV [P1:gerjuoy_stein_1955]; Glauber/long-range-only models underestimate at 10-50 eV [P1:gianturco_lamanna_rahman].
Song 2023 Table 4 (measured-based vibrationally elastic ICS to 1000 eV, 10-20 %) bounds the rotational sum only by inference [P1:song2023_jpcrd].
sub_material_changes: Open theory coverage extends from 10 eV to 50 eV (lane-01 had none above 10 eV).
Evidence (theory only) that the flat hold is not conservative channel by channel and that a two-transition table is incomplete above ~30 eV (j0->6).
Access facts: Itikawa et al. 1986 and Majeed & Strickland 1997 full texts are openly available as NIST SRD JPCRD reprints (lane-01 labelled them not accessed / abstract only).

adversarial_check.assessment: Both findings are substantially accurate; no fabricated source was found. The confirmed openly accessible new evidence is theory-only above 10 eV. It consists of Itikawa et al. 1986 Table 5.1 (Onda & Truhlar; Rumble, Truhlar & Morrison: j0->2/4/6 to 50 eV), Siegel, Dehmer & Dill 1978 (to 30 eV), and one preliminary, unpublished measurement (Tanaka et al. 1980, via Itikawa 1986) to 20 eV, which the compilers themselves say 'have to be confirmed'. Every source whose range reaches the lane-01 E_req is closed and abstract-only: Kutz & Meyer 1995 (0.01-1000 eV), Bhattacharyya & Goswami 1982 (20-200 eV), Gote & Ehrhardt 1995 (the only measurement, DCS 10-200 eV) and Choi et al. 1979 (50-500 eV). The E_req is ~266 eV for 1 % at L = 60 eV, 668 eV at 1e-6 and 1244 eV at 1e-12. With accessible coverage ending at 50 eV, 50.8 % (L = 45) and 64.8 % (L = 60) of the held j0->2 rate still lies above the last covered point, far outside the 1 % convention. The confirmed data do usefully show three things: the 10 eV join with Song Table 6 is 1.2-1.4x low for j0->2; the flat hold is not conservative channel by channel (j0->2 falls about 2x by 50 eV, j0->4 rises, j0->6 appears); and a two-transition table is likely incomplete above ~30 eV. These are indicators about the current declared model, not a closure of the gap. Rotational remains UNRESOLVED-BY-SOURCE for any domain extension, and the structural blocker (<= 37 of 714 v1 OOD runs) is unchanged. Material improvement is NOT confirmed. Legitimate library or purchase access to Kutz & Meyer, Gote & Ehrhardt and Bhattacharyya & Goswami is an owner decision. This check changes no table, limit, pre-registration or v1 result, and does not decide Question A.

Openly accessible evidence found here extends coverage to 50 eV only, and only as theory: Itikawa et al. 1986 Table 5.1 (Onda & Truhlar; Rumble, Truhlar & Morrison; 10-50 eV, j0->2/4/6) and Siegel, Dehmer & Dill 1978 (to 30 eV), plus one preliminary, unpublished measurement to 20 eV (Tanaka et al. 1980, via Itikawa 1986). With the table's own hold envelope, the share of the j0->2 Maxwellian rate from energies above 50 eV is 50.8 % at L = 45 eV and 64.8 % at L = 60 eV (above 20 eV: 91.4 % at L = 60), against the 1 % C1 convention (j0->4: 48.4 % and 63.0 %). Reaching C1 at L = 60 eV needs cross sections to about 266 eV (share above 266 eV = 0.99 %); coverage to 200 eV would satisfy 1 % only at L = 45 eV (0.98 %; 4.06 % at L = 60). The only sources whose stated ranges reach 200-1000 eV - Kutz & Meyer 1995 (theory, ICS 0.001-1000 eV), Bhattacharyya & Goswami 1982 (eikonal theory without exchange, ICS 20-200 eV), Choi et al. 1979 (two-potential theory, 50-500 eV, rotational content unclear) and Gote & Ehrhardt 1995 (the only measurement: state-to-state DCS 10-200 eV, 10-160 deg) - are closed access (abstract only; paywall or bot challenge, not bypassed). Under the measured-only reading nothing measurement-based beyond 20 eV is accessible, so C1 coverage stays at 10 eV (20 eV if a conference-abstract measurement were admitted). None of the 1e-6 / 1e-12 E_req (575-668 / 1154-1244 eV) is reached by any accessible source. (2) Join (C3). Every independent value at 10 eV lies above Song Table 6: j0->2 1.22x (Onda), 1.22x (Rumble), 1.44x (Siegel), 1.40x (Tanaka prelim. exp.), 1.26-1.27x (Burke & Chandra 1972; Chandra & Temkin 1976, via Siegel Table 2); j0->4 1.47x / 1.08x / 1.12x / 0.87x. Neither Song nor these sources states an uncertainty (Itikawa 1986 says calculations scatter by more than a factor of 2), so C3 cannot be evaluated as defined. (3) Shape (C2). The accessible theory contradicts the flat hold. From 10 to 50 eV j0->2 falls to 0.42-0.43 of its 10 eV value, j0->4 dips (0.59-0.87 at 20 eV) then rises to 1.0-1.4x at 50 eV, and j0->6 - not in the table set - grows to 0.24-0.34e-16 cm2 at 30-50 eV; Kutz & Meyer and Gote & Ehrhardt (abstracts) report rotational rainbows / large angular-momentum transfer at higher energy. Replacing the hold by the theory shape (scaled at 10 eV) on 10-50 eV only, keeping the hold beyond, changes the table rate at L = 60 eV by -9.73 % / -9.59 % (j0->2, Onda / Rumble) and -5.32 % / 8.09 % (j0->4) - all beyond the 1 % C2 threshold; if the scaled 50 eV theory value is held beyond 50 eV (instead of Song's 10 eV value), j0->2 changes by -47.1 % and j0->4 by -4.86 % to 34.8 %. The omitted j0->6 channel alone is 7.30 %-8.10 % of the j0->2 table's collision rate at L = 60 eV (absolute theory values, held beyond 50 eV). Rotational energy loss per event is only 1.5-4.9 meV (10 meV for j0->6), so the gap matters for the activity-based f_out domain classification, not for the power balance. So the hold is neither an upper nor a lower envelope transition by transition, and a two-transition table is incomplete above ~30 eV. These are theory-only indicators (no verdicts, no table change). (4) Independence. Onda & Truhlar and Rumble et al. share the Truhlar group lineage; Siegel et al. use a different (multiple-scattering) model; all are independent of Song's R-matrix. None is independent measurement above 20 eV. (5) Theory-only envelope (D-X8). A Born point-quadrupole (Gerjuoy-Stein) envelope is not supported as a bound: its energy-independent high-energy j0->2 value (~0.34e-16 cm2 for Q = 1.045 e a0^2; formula from memory: verify) is ~9x below Song at 10 eV and ~5x below the 50 eV theory, and Magboltz-type constructions extend it above 5 eV by an assumed elastic-MTCS fall-off. Net: the evidence base improved from 10 to 50 eV (theory) and now documents that the held tail is not conservative for j0->4/j0->6, but it does not come close to the energy coverage the lane-01 requirements need, rotational stays UNRESOLVED-BY-SOURCE under the stated criteria, and the structural blocker (at most 37 of 714 v1 OOD runs recoverable with the rotational cap) is unchanged. Legitimate next steps are owner decisions: library or purchased access to Kutz & Meyer 1995, Gote & Ehrhardt 1995, Bhattacharyya & Goswami 1982, Choi et al. 1979, Itikawa & Mason 2005 and Itikawa 2006 (no author contact, no LXCat). Nothing here changes any table, validity limit, pre-registration or v1 result, and whether Question A's reopening condition is met is the owner's decision.

search_log.finder_gap_assessment: NOT MATERIALLY CLOSED. (1) New openly accessible independent evidence above 10 eV: three model-derived theory sets - Onda & Truhlar 1979/80 (close coupling) and Rumble, Truhlar & Morrison 1983 (FN + sudden, HF potentials), both reproduced in Itikawa et al. 1986 JPCRD Table 5.1 (NIST SRD public reprint), and Siegel, Dehmer & Dill 1978 ANL-78-65 Table 1 (OSTI full text) - give sigma(0->2,4,6) to 50 eV (SDD to 30 eV); plus one preliminary, unconfirmed measurement (Tanaka, Boesten & Shimamura 1980) to 20 eV. The Onda-Truhlar abstract confirms the Table 5.1 sums (5.21 vs 5.217; 3.28 vs 3.268 x1e-16 cm2). Song 2023 Table 4 (measured vibrationally elastic ICS, 10-20 %, to 1000 eV) is only an UPPER BOUND on the rotational sum (Itikawa 1986 Sec. 4/5.3: beam 'elastic' includes rotational transitions); theory rot-sum/vib-elastic = 0.38-0.52 at 10-50 eV. (2) Coverage (C1-type): the last covered point moves from 10 eV to 50 eV (theory reading) or 20 eV (preliminary measurement). Share of the committed table's rate above 50 eV: j0->2 50.8 % (L=45), 64.8 % (60), 79.9 % (90), 91.1 % (150); j0->4 48.4/63.0/78.8/90.6 %. Even with the independent theory shape and a falling (vibrationally-elastic-shaped) tail, 42.8 % (j0->2, L=60) of the rate lies above 50 eV, and E_req is still 216-229 eV (1 %), 594-607 eV (1e-6), 1155-1168 eV (1e-12) at L=60 (hold envelope: 266/668/1244 eV). No accessible rotational sigma exists above 50 eV, so C1 fails at every L >= 45 eV in both readings; under the measured reading nothing counts above 20 eV (and that point is preliminary). (3) Join/shape (C3/C2-type): at the 10 eV join table/theory = 0.82 (OT), 0.82 (Rumble), 0.69 (SDD), 0.72 (Tanaka prelim.) for 0->2 and 0.68/0.93/0.89/1.15 for 0->4; no stated uncertainty exists for any theory set (Itikawa 1986: calculated rotational cross sections 'scatter by more than a factor of 2'), so C3 cannot be evaluated under the lane-01 rule (owner decision 4). The three independent sets agree with each other (0->2 within ~20 %) but not with the held table: held sigma(0->2) is 1.92-1.93x both CC sets at 50 eV, held sigma(0->4) is 0.53-0.84x at 30-50 eV, and the held 0->2+0->4 (4.07) exceeds the measured vibrationally elastic ICS itself above ~160 eV (physically impossible). Replacing the hold by the independent shapes changes the j0->2 rate by -29 % to -47 % at L=45 eV and -31 % to -55 % at L=60 eV (j0->4: -19 % to +50 % at L=45, depending on set, normalisation and tail), i.e. C2 fails by roughly 30-55x the 1 % tolerance. This is context about the declared-model hold INSIDE the current 45 eV cap (rotational energy loss is only 1.5-4.9 meV, so the physical power effect is negligible, but the validity-limit bookkeeping is affected); it changes no v1 table, limit, status or result. (4) Sources that could close the gap exist but are not openly accessible: Kutz & Meyer 1995 (theory, 0.01-1000 eV; would meet 1 % coverage up to L ~ 150 eV and 1e-6 up to L ~ 90 eV, not 1e-12 beyond L ~ 50-60 eV; theory-only, independent of Song), Gote & Ehrhardt 1995 (the only MEASUREMENT above 20 eV: state-to-state DCS 10-200 eV, 10-160 deg; ICS would need angular extrapolation; reaches only the L ~ 45 eV 1 % requirement), Bhattacharyya & Goswami 1982 (eikonal, ICS 20-200 eV), Gupta & Mathur 1981 (10-100 eV, tuned to experiment). Whether to obtain them through legitimate library/purchase access is owner decision 5. Itikawa 2006, Itikawa & Mason 2005 and Kawaguchi 2021 remain inaccessible. The Gerjuoy-Stein quadrupole Born estimate is confirmed (abstract) to be a slow-electron threshold theory, not a usable envelope above 10 eV. (5) Verdict for P1: the rotational tables stay UNRESOLVED-BY-SOURCE for any extension; the structural blocker (<= 37 of 714 v1 OOD runs recoverable with the rotational cap) is unchanged. The new evidence materially improves knowledge of the 10-50 eV shape (and indicates the current hold is biased high for j0->2 above ~30 eV and low for j0->4), but it does not provide cross sections over the energy range the lane-01 requirements need. Whether the Question A reopening condition is met is the owner's decision; this search changes no table, limit, pre-registration or v1 result. For A, W, B', a' and w no measurement or calculation above 100 eV was found at all (B3Pi_g emission to 450 eV was REJECTED by the check: the 450 eV range belongs to N2+ bands).

Only two open evaluated sets reach above 100 eV for all eight states: Majeed & Strickland 1997 (full text open; built on Cartwright 1977 ICS measured at 10-50 eV, not renormalized, extrapolated by an undocumented method, no uncertainty) [P2:majeed_strickland1997] and the Kawaguchi 2018 thesis set (swarm-adjusted, anchored on Johnson at 100 eV, extrapolated above; identity with PSST 2021 not verified) [P2:kawaguchi2018_thesis]. Neither is measured above 100 eV, and they disagree (thesis/repo continuation 0.29-1.42 at 400-1000 eV).

a1Pi_g: Ajello et al. 2020 gives an inferred, EEL-independent 200 eV point, 4.2e-18 cm2 = 1.23x Johnson (3.41 +- 0.87e-18), composite ~35 % [P2:ajello2020]. Measurements above 200 eV exist only as abstracts: Oda & Osawa 1981 (EEL-GOS, 500-2000 eV) [P2:oda_osawa1981], Skerbele & Lassettre 1970 (DCS/GOS 300-500 eV, Born holds) [P2:skerbele_lassettre1970], Holland 1969 (apparent LBH emission, 900 eV absolute, shape to 2 keV) [P2:holland1969]; Chung & Lin 1972 (Born-Ochkur to 2 keV for singlets) is theory [P2:chung_lin1972]. Ajello & Shemansky 1985 (open reprint) has measured data only to 200 eV plus an analytic fit [P2:ajello_shemansky1985].

search_log.finder_gap_assessment: NOT materially closed. (1) a1Pi_g above 200 eV: the lane-01 candidate 'Ajello & Shemansky 1985' is now read in full (open reprint) and contains measured data only to 200 eV plus an analytic fit, so it does not extend measured coverage. Genuinely independent a1Pi_g evidence above 200 eV exists in the primary literature - Holland 1969 (apparent LBH emission, absolute at 900 eV, energy dependence to 2 keV), Skerbele & Lassettre 1970 (absolute EELS DCS/GOS at 300-500 eV, Born valid), Chung & Lin 1972 (Born-Ochkur to 2 keV, 25 % vs experiment at 900 eV) - but all three are abstract-only here (AIP/APS 403, ADS human-verification, not bypassed), so no tabulated cross sections with uncertainties can be used. Where the abstracts give numbers they point to a CONFLICT: Holland's apparent sigma(900)/sigma(100) = 0.164 and sigma(2000)/sigma(100) = 0.078 against 0.095 and 0.041 for the v1 table continuation (~1.7-1.9x), which is only partly attributable to cascade. (2) The seven other states above 100 eV: C3Pi_u has independent optical measurements to 600 eV (Fons 1996, 13-20 %) and 1000 eV (Imami & Borst 1974, whose absolute scale is ~10x below others by the authors' own statement), and B3Pi_g has apparent 1PG emission to ~450 eV (Stanton & St John 1969, cascade-laden). All are abstract-only, and the B data cannot give a direct ICS without a cascade model. For A3Sigma_u+, W3Delta_u, B'3Sigma_u- and a'1Sigma_u- no measurement or calculation above 100 eV was found. For w1Delta_u only a Born calculation (Chung & Lin, abstract-only) was found. Open-access sets that span keV energies (Nicolanti 2023 CC BY; Jain & Bhardwaj 2011) are analytic fits to <= 100 eV data, not independent evidence. Kawaguchi 2021 is still paywalled; OpenAlex's OA flag was wrong. (3) Conflicts: nothing resolves the Johnson/MS1997 100 eV disagreement (factors 0.17-3.8) for A, B, W, B', a', w, C. Two independent indicators partly bear on it. Kato et al. 2010 support the JPL/CSUF DCS behind Johnson for a1Pi_g and C3Pi_u, but only at 20-40 eV. Ajello et al. 2017 (open) measure a cascade into a1Pi_g at 100 eV of >= 3.3e-18 cm2, about 3x both Johnson's a'+w (1.00e-18) and the MS1997-implied a'+w (~1.09e-18). That suggests both sets are low for a'+w, or that higher states also feed the cascade; it does not arbitrate between them. The Ajello 2020 cascade values at 200 eV (abstract-only) would be the only a'/w handle above 100 eV. Overall: nothing found supplies accessible cross sections, with stated uncertainty, from an independent source, to the lane-01 E_req (~575-650 eV at the 1e-6 level, >= 1.15 keV at 1e-12) for any of the eight tables, and nothing resolves the conflicts. The search produced candidate evidence for a future full-text-access request (owner decision 5 in the audit: library/purchase, no bypass): Holland 1969, Skerbele & Lassettre 1970, Chung & Lin 1972, Fons 1996, Ajello et al. 2020, plus Kawaguchi 2021. It also produced two new conflict indicators (Holland's high-energy a1Pi_g shape; Ajello 2017 a'+w cascade). Whether any of this meets the Question A reopening condition is the owner's decision.

(9) background is vibrationally elastic only) [P3:laporta2014].

The only new, confirmed, openly accessible quantitative evidence is Itikawa et al. 1986 Fig. 6.1: two renormalized Truhlar et al. 1977 measured 0->1 points, ~9e-19 cm2 at ~50 eV and ~6.7e-19 cm2 at ~75 eV, digitized (+/-10-15 %), no stated uncertainty, same Itikawa/JPL lineage as the Tabata fit (not independent) [P3:itikawa1986, P3:truhlar1977].

No measured non-resonant 0->1 value above ~75 eV and no non-resonant overtone measurement exist in the accessible literature (Itikawa 1986 Sec. 6.2); theory to 500 eV (Choi et al. 1979) is abstract-only and model-derived [P3:choi1979]. search_log.finder_gap_assessment: NOT materially closed. What the evidence establishes: (1) The component that the resonant-only Laporta tables omit above ~5 eV is physically two things: the 2Sigma_u shape resonance peaking at ~20-22 eV (FWHM ~7 eV; Tanaka 1981, Burke 1983, Gillan 1987, Malegat 1988) and polarization-dominated non-resonant scattering at >= ~33 eV (Truhlar 1972, 1977). Laporta 2014 excludes both by construction (Eq. 9 background is vibrationally elastic only). (2) Measured-lineage 0->1 integral values exist only to ~75 eV: Tanaka 1981 (3-30 eV, +/-30 % as adopted by Itikawa 2006) and Truhlar et al. 1976/1977 renormalized by Trajmar 1983, visible (not tabulated) in the openly accessible Itikawa 1986 Fig. 6.1 (~50 eV 8.9e-19, ~74 eV 6.7e-19 cm2, digitized here). The QST/Tabata fit used by lane-01 stops at 48.5 eV and drops the ~75 eV point. Adding it narrows the lane-01 bracket for the omitted non-resonant 0->1 rate / table rate from 2.05-2.50 to 2.22-2.39 at T_e 30 eV and from 2.91-5.56 to 3.35-4.86 at T_e 60 eV (tails beyond 75 eV: zero / held / 1/E / lnE/E). Beyond 75 eV there is no measurement and only abstract-level theory (polarized Born to 83 eV), so E_req (~575 eV at 1e-6, >= 1.15 keV at 1e-12) is not met. (3) Overtones: no measurement outside the 2Pi_g region (Itikawa 1986 Sec. 6.2 says so explicitly); theory (Rumble 1983, Burke 1983 via Itikawa 1986 Table 6.1) gives 0->2/0->1 ~0.03-0.34 at 20-30 eV and ~0.03 at 50 eV; theory magnitudes are 2-5x off the measured 0->1 at 30-50 eV. (4) Independence: the 50-75 eV points share the Itikawa 1986/Trajmar-JPL lineage with the Tabata fit; the one potentially independent measurement at 20-50 eV (Middleton, Brunger & Teubner 1992) and the only recent study (Martendal & Mazon 2022) were not accessible (bot challenge / closed). No stated uncertainty accessible above 30 eV. (5) Materiality context, indicative only (my arithmetic, not a verdict): scaling the repository's final-audit numbers (F_P_vib = 3.3e-4 at T_e 30 eV, audit/n2_completeness_final_v1.json; 0->1 = 21.7 % of the resonant vibrational power from the committed tables) by the 2.2-2.4 ratio gives a non-resonant 0->1 F_P of ~1.6-1.7e-4 at T_e 30 eV, ~2e-4 with a theory-bounded overtone allowance, i.e. well below the pre-registered 1 % F_P promotion threshold even with a factor-5 margin. The completeness re-audit (a pre-registered owner process, not this search) is where that bound would have to be made with a denominator above T_e 30 eV. So the new evidence modestly tightens and documents the P3 magnitude to ~75 eV, but supplies no independent, uncertainty-stated cross sections over the energy range the lane-01 requirements need. Whether this meets the Question A reopening condition is the owner's decision.

search_log.finder_gap_assessment: Not materially closed. Lane-01 needs non-resonant v=0->1 (and overtone) cross sections to at least ~575 eV (1e-6 share) with stated uncertainty from an independent source. What exists: (a) measured ICS to ~75 eV only (Truhlar et al. 1977, renormalized by Trajmar 1983), accessible only as a digitized point in the open Itikawa 1986 Fig. 6.1 (~0.9e-18 cm2 at ~50 eV, ~0.7e-18 at ~75 eV; reading error ~10-15 %; no stated uncertainty); (b) calculations to 50 eV (Rumble 1983, Onda & Truhlar 1979) that exceed that measurement by ~2.5x at 50 eV, which is a new conflict; (c) theory nominally to 500-800 eV (Choi et al. 1979; Lee & Freitas 1983) that is abstract-only or not accessed, and would be model-derived anyway. The newest evaluation (Song 2023) recommends only Laporta's resonant data and has no >5 eV component. What does improve: the 75 eV point shows the non-resonant component continues above the Tabata n2-5 fit's 48.5 eV end and falls slowly (about E^-0.7 between 50 and 75 eV). So the audit's two bounds become a real bracket: 'zero beyond 48.5 eV' (2.05x table at T_e 30) is too low, and 'held beyond 48.5 eV' (2.50x) is too high. Illustrative model-derived arithmetic (mine, not a table change): a power-law tail E^-0.7 to E^-1 from 48.5 eV keeps 0.62-0.71 of the held tail's Maxwellian weight at T_e 30 eV. That gives about 2.3-2.4x the table's 0->1 rate at T_e 30 eV, 0.44-0.56 of the held tail at T_e 60, and 0.33-0.44 at T_e 100. The asymptotic slope beyond 75 eV is unmeasured; a Born ~ln(E)/E form is from memory, verify. Overtones: calculated 0->2/0->1 is ~0.03 at 50 eV (Rumble), so they are likely minor non-resonantly (model-derived). Net: the finding strengthens the case that non-resonant excitation is a real omitted channel with magnitude at T_e 30 eV of about 2.3x the table's 0->1 rate (within the existing bracket). It does not supply the cross sections above ~75 eV that a domain extension needs. Whether this meets the Question A reopening condition is the owner's decision.
